title: The sync gate runs a code change's own test files with their git scenarios, not every test file that reaches it
goal: Under the sync gate (tests.py --changed REV with KB_TESTS_FAST=1) a changed tool module selects only the test files that import it or name its script themselves (testmap.direct_refs, depth 1), each with its git scenarios, plus the source scans (TOOL_SCANS), the tools-map test, the leak scan and TestCloudInGit for kbgit.py and querylog.py as today; a test file that reaches the module only through other modules runs in the full tests.py of the sprint's review story instead; testmap.py explain names each file's reason; a bl_base.py change selects 9 test files plus the scans instead of 71 nodes that keep their git scenarios; planted cases: a test file reaching the module only through another module is left out, one importing it is selected with its git scenarios

gates.question: Which test files does the sync gate run, with their git scenarios, for a changed tool module? direct-only = only the test files that import or name the module themselves, with their git scenarios, plus the source scans, the tools-map test, the leak scan and TestCloudInGit; files reaching it through other modules wait for the review's full run (est. 1-3 min macOS, 3-6 min Windows per code gate). direct = every reaching file as today, but only the direct ones keep their git scenarios (est. 4-5 min macOS, 10-13 min Windows). no-git = every reaching file without any git scenario but TestCloudInGit for kbgit.py and querylog.py (at most the 238 s median of an all gate on macOS). keep = today's closure with git scenarios (median 507 s macOS)

notes: Premise (run before a sprint commits it): python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import tests; r = tests.plan(['_tools/bl_base.py'], True); print(len(r), len(r[0][0]), repr(r[0][1]))" prints 1 71 'not stress': one run of 71 nodes, every one keeping its git scenarios. Data, committed ops sidecars 2026-10-02 to 10-05 (macOS host): 401 sync.gate rows; the 99 of scope changed-git (code changes) took median 507 s, p90 839 s, 777 of the 888 gate test minutes (87%); the 8 of scope all (every file, no git scenarios) median 238 s, so a typical code gate costs twice an all gate; in the slow gates test_querylog_e2e.py holds 22% of the worker time, test_backlog.py 16%, test_sync.py 10%, test_ql_deliver.py 10%, test_kbpublic.py 8%, and each reaches over 60 tool modules. Live run of the map over the repository: the 382 code merges since 2026-10-01 select a median of 74 of 103 test files (p90 89); over 16 common modules (bl_land, bl_base, kg_sync, ql_capture, kbcommon, check, rag, kbgit, backlog, querylog, tests and others) the reaching test files sum to 1146 and the directly importing or naming ones to 242 (bl_land 46 to 15, bl_base 70 to 9, kg_sync 70 to 13, ql_capture 82 to 17). Estimate, not measured: a code gate falls from about 8.5 min to 1 to 3 min on macOS, and from about 20 to 25 min to 3 to 6 min on the Windows host (its full suite runs about 2.5 times slower). Coverage moves, not lost: the review story's full tests.py still runs every git scenario once per sprint. Options other than direct-only reshape the goal: direct keeps every reaching file but without git scenarios beyond the direct ones; no-git drops every git scenario but TestCloudInGit.
